props.title: Flatliners
props.initialSlug: Med students tempt death to glimpse the afterlife

sections.content: Flatliners (1990) launched a fascinating wave of psychological horror-thrillers exploring near-death experiences through a scientific lens. Joel Schumacher's stylish direction creates a neo-Gothic atmosphere where ambitious medical students experiment with controlled death. The film's visual aesthetic - all shadowy cathedral-like spaces and neon-lit operating rooms - influenced later medical thrillers like Extreme Measures (1996) and Awake (2007). Kiefer Sutherland leads a stellar young cast including Julia Roberts and Kevin Bacon, capturing the hubris of brilliant minds pushing ethical boundaries.

sections.content: The film's exploration of guilt, redemption, and the consequences of playing god resonates with other metaphysical thrillers of the era. Ghost (1990) and Jacob's Ladder (1990) similarly dealt with the intersection of death and psychological trauma, while Altered States (1980) preceded Flatliners in showing scientists pushing themselves to dangerous extremes. The practical effects and surreal nightmare sequences hold up remarkably well, creating genuinely unsettling moments without relying on gore.

The 2017 remake of Flatliners attempted to update the concept with modern technology but missed the original's compelling mix of existential dread and character development. The original succeeded by keeping its focus tight on the psychological toll of the experiments rather than explaining the metaphysics. This approach influenced later films like The Lazarus Effect (2015) and Lucy (2014), which similarly deal with humans pushing beyond normal consciousness. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

movies.title: Event Horizon
movies.slug: A rescue crew investigates a spaceship that disappeared into a supernatural dimension

sections.content: Flatliners helped establish a template for science-gone-wrong thrillers that combine elements of horror with legitimate scientific concepts. Films like Hollow Man (2000) and Event Horizon (1997) followed its lead in using cutting-edge science as a launching pad for supernatural horror. The film's emphasis on hubris and redemption also influenced psychological thrillers like A Cure for Wellness (2016) and Shutter Island (2010).
